title: Gideon and the Well
premise: When pest controller Quentin Eriksen is hired to deal with an infestation at the Hollowmere farmstead, he finds no vermin—only doors that count themselves, lights that stay on for something unseen, and fingerprints on the ceiling that match no living hand. Beneath the property, an excavation crew has broken into a stone door sealed from the inside, releasing a presence that harvests households one member at a time. Quentin and the surviving Eriksen family must reverse the count—getting every living soul out ahead of the harvest moon—or become the well's next inheritance. In the end, Quentin seals himself inside with the thing, trading his name for theirs, and the farm goes dark forever.
about_author: Xanthe Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former rural insurance adjuster who spent a decade documenting claims no actuary could explain. They write horror from a farmhouse in undisclosed northern country, where they keep meticulous records of their own doors.

chapters.title: The Call-Out
chapters.summary: Quentin Eriksen, third-generation pest controller, takes a routine job at the Hollowmere farm after the owner reports scratching inside the walls. His POV establishes his methodical rituals: counting doors, logging lights. He finds droppings that are warm, arranged in rows of seven. The beat is professional unease curdling into personal investment.

chapters.title: Fingerprints on the Ceiling
chapters.summary: Quentin returns at dusk to set traps and discovers handprints pressed into the kitchen ceiling—small, human, five-fingered, too many joints. The farmer's daughter, Maren, admits she's been counting them; there were four yesterday, six today. POV shifts briefly to Maren. The emotional beat: a child's calm acceptance terrifying an adult.

chapters.title: Lights That Stay On
chapters.summary: Quentin installs monitoring equipment. Every night at 3:11 a.m., the porch light switches itself on and stays lit until dawn, as if keeping watch or waiting. His own apartment light begins doing the same. POV: Quentin, fraying. The beat: the infestation has learned his address.

chapters.title: The Excavation Crew
chapters.summary: A county crew digging a drainage trench behind Hollowmere strikes dressed stone twelve feet down—a door, iron-banded, sealed from the inside with molten lead poured through the keyhole. Foreman Dale Okafor narrates his crew's giddy excitement. The beat: triumph before catastrophe, the reader screaming inwardly.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Dale's crew cuts the lead seal overnight against Quentin's warnings. Inside: a dry stone shaft descending past torch brackets, and at the bottom, a well mouth breathing cold air upward in slow, tidal exhalations. One worker, Petra, hears her dead brother call her name. Beat: grief weaponized as bait.

chapters.title: The First Taken
chapters.summary: Petra descends alone on camera and doesn't come back up; the feed shows her walking down, then nothing, then her flashlight rising without her. Quentin arrives to find police treating it as a fall. He counts the farmhouse doors: thirteen outside, fourteen inside. Beat: denial meeting arithmetic.

chapters.title: Doors That Count Themselves
chapters.summary: Quentin maps the house and finds new doorways appearing where walls were solid—an extra closet, a second pantry, each opening onto darkness that smells of well water. Maren helps him chalk-number every threshold. Her POV reveals she's known about the counting since her mother vanished years ago. Beat: inherited dread.

chapters.title: What the Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Quentin locates the family matriarch, Ilse Eriksen—no relation he can prove—in a care home. She explains the Hollowmere covenant: the well beneath takes a tithe each generation, and the house's doors multiply as it prepares the harvest. She gives him her father's ledger of names paid. Beat: exposition as wound.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: The ledger lists every household at Hollowmere since 1847, each entry ending mid-name—the final letters scratched out. Quentin realizes the missing letters spell the taken, and the last page has begun writing itself: D-A-L-E. Dale Okafor's POV: he wakes unable to remember the last three letters of his own surname. Beat: identity eroding.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Ilse calculates the cycle: the well completes its taking when the harvest moon crests the water tower, nine nights out. Whatever remains inside the count by then belongs to it permanently. Quentin proposes the impossible: get every living person off the ledger before moonrise. Beat: grim resolve forming a plan.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: Quentin moves the remaining crew and the Hollowmere family into a motel, but the count follows—doors in the motel hallway, the porch light burning in the parking lot. Maren's little brother Tomas sleepwalks toward the stairwell each night, whispering numbers downward. Beat: sanctuary failing; nowhere is outside the property line.

chapters.title: The Tithe Refused
chapters.summary: Quentin theorizes the well must be offered someone willingly or it reaches for everyone. He attempts to negotiate at the shaft mouth, reading names from the ledger aloud, offering himself. The well answers with his own voice, reciting his childhood address. Beat: hubris and terror; the thing already owns pieces of him.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren, who has heard the well all her life, secretly offers herself—it took her mother; she wants to see her. Quentin catches her at the shaft edge at 3:11 a.m. Their confrontation exposes the theme: survival's price is always someone else's name. Beat: heartbreak; he pulls her back but the ledger gains her first letter anyway.

chapters.title: Fourteen Doors
chapters.summary: The farmhouse now contains fourteen doors where thirteen should be, and the fourteenth stands open in Quentin's rented room, exhaling cold. Inside it, faintly, Petra's voice counts aloud—downward. Quentin understands the taken aren't dead; they're inventory. Beat: hope curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: With two nights left, Quentin goes down the shaft with rope, chalk, and the ledger, leaving instructions: if he isn't up by moonrise, burn the farmhouse and salt the ground. The descent chapters shift fully to his claustrophobic POV. At the bottom, the well mouth is a doorway now, standing open. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Counting Room
chapters.summary: Below, Quentin finds a chamber lined with doors—hundreds, salvaged from every era of the farm—and behind each, a voice counting. He finds Petra, alive but translucent, mid-count, unable to stop. She begs him not to say her name; naming completes the entry. Beat: horror of recognition without rescue.

chapters.title: The Well Speaks
chapters.summary: The presence manifests as every prior owner of Hollowmere, wearing their faces like borrowed coats, and offers Quentin the old covenant: give it a name freely given, and the rest go free. It shows him the alternative—the harvest moon taking the whole motel. Beat: temptation made explicit; power's corrupting offer.

chapters.title: What Quentin Decides
chapters.summary: Quentin realizes the covenant's loophole: the ledger erases what it's given, so he offers not his life but his name—his identity, his record, his place in the world—to be written into the well forever while his body walks out empty. The owners laugh, then consider. Beat: sacrifice reframed as cleverness, with dread underneath.

chapters.title: Moonrise
chapters.summary: As the harvest moon crests the water tower, Quentin speaks the bargain aloud at the shaft bottom. The chamber doors slam open; Petra and the taken pour upward as light. Above, the family watches the farmhouse's extra doors vanish one by one. Beat: climax—simultaneous release above and surrender below.

chapters.title: The Empty Man
chapters.summary: Quentin climbs out at dawn, alive, but when Maren greets him he looks through her—the ledger took his name, memories of self unraveling hour by hour. He retains only procedure: counting doors, checking lights. The family vows to keep him, arguing over whether a man without a name is still owed anything. Beat: bittersweet cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Keeping the Lights On
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the Hollowmere household runs on quiet ritual: Maren counts the doors (always thirteen), Tomas checks the porch light, and Quentin—called only 'the keeper'—performs his rounds with serene precision. The well is silent, the shaft filled with lead poured from the inside this time. Beat: fragile peace, tenderness in routine.

chapters.title: The Sixteenth Door
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Maren's POV: on the autumn equinox she finds a sixteenth door chalk-marked in handwriting she almost recognizes, and the ledger's last page shows a fresh entry beginning—not a name, but a title: THE KEEPER. She closes the book, keeps the light on, and starts teaching Tomas the count. Beat: inheritance continuing; the price was never paid once, only deferred.
